title: The Relentless Two-Envelope Conundrum: A Paradox or a Misapplication of Probability Theory
content: The Two-Envelope Problem (TEP) is revisited to argue that the traditional evaluation of expected returns is based on spurious probabilities arising from a misapplication of formal probability theory. The source of the problem lies in the probabilistic framing of the two identical envelopes, X and Y, one containing twice as much money as the other. After one envelope has been selected, say X, and its content X=x revealed, the value x is then used to define Y in terms of the values y=x/2 and y=2x, each assigned probability .5, and vice versa when Y is selected. This ex post framing – after X=x is revealed – engenders the familiar paradox by rendering X and Y ill-defined random variables from a formal probabilistic perspective. The paradox disappears when the TEP is framed in the context of axiomatic probability by defining the random variables X and Y in terms of the unknown contents of the two envelopes, say $θ and $2θ. Their probabilistic dependence is accounted for by assigning the pairs of values (x=θ , y=2θ) and (x=2θ , y=θ) to specify their joint distribution. This distribution gives rise to identical expected returns for the two envelopes, implying indifference between keeping the chosen envelope and switching, unraveling the alleged paradox.
